text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the same prophets of doom who predicted that the economy would overheat due to rapid growth, are now trying to undermine the economy simply to prove their predictions were right.

-- The government plans to develop Malay reserve land in the near future with non-Malays given the option to lease it for a maximum of 30 years, said Deputy Land and Cooperative Development Minister Goh Cheng Teik.
-- Ekran Bhd 's general manager for corporate finance Tang Yow Sai said it was optimistic of achieveing its forecast after-tax profit of 240.16 million ringgit for the year ended June 30, 1998.
-- The Cabinet has directed the Works Ministry to study whether highway toll rates can be reduecd, said Works Minister Samy Vellu.

-- Telekom Malaysia 's foreign loan exposure may cost the utility an additional 60 million ringgit in its current financial year due to the ringgit's depreciation, said its head of corporate treasury Ghazali Harun.

-- The International Monetary Fund says it should be included in any Southeast Asian arangement to deal with problems arising from the currency turmoil facing the region, said director of IMF regional office for Asia and the Pacific, Kunio Saito.
